title: Milk Bread Pull-Apart Rolls
description: Soft, fluffy Japanese-style milk bread rolls made with tangzhong for an airy texture and longer freshness.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.quantity: 4 tablespoons, room temperature, plus more for greasing

steps.instruction: Make the tangzhong by whisking 2 tablespoons flour with 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon milk in a small saucepan until smooth.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, until thickened and a spoon leaves a clear trail on the bottom of the pan, about 3 minutes.
Transfer the tangzhong to a bowl and let it cool to room temperature.
In a stand mixer bowl, combine 2 1/2 cups flour, sugar, yeast, and salt.
Add the warm milk, egg, and cooled tangzhong. Mix on low speed until a soft dough forms, about 3 minutes.
Switch to the dough hook, add the butter pieces, and mix until incorporated.
Increase speed to medium-high and knead until the dough is smooth, soft, and tacky, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Transfer the dough to a lightly buttered bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
Gently deflate the dough and divide it into 8 equal pieces.
Shape each piece into a tight ball or knot and arrange in the prepared pan with space between each piece.
Cover and let rise again until puffy, 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Whisk together the remaining egg and 1 tablespoon milk to make the egg wash.
Brush the tops of the rolls with the egg wash.
Bake for about 25 minutes until golden brown.
Cool in the pan for 15 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
